newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to charge on, aim for 114-31 peak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to charge on, aim for 114-31 peak.

text.p: September gilt futures on LIFFE will look to build on Tuesday's strength and eventually gain a foothold around the May peak of 114-31, chart analysts said on Wednesday.
After gaining almost a point on Tuesday to close at 113-23, gilts could test resistance initially at 114-00 before recapturing the contract high of 114-31 on May 9, analysts said.

"We're now starting to point back up. Slow stochastics are pointing that way...probably between now and Friday's U.S. payrolls data it will squeeze a little bit higher," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank in London.
At 0700 GMT, the September gilt future opened 3/32 down at 113-20.
Beauchamp said gilts would first try to overcome the area around 114-00 which was marked by a high of 114-02 on May 19, and a low of 113-30 on June 3.
The market would then charge towards the high of 114-31.

"Potentially we have got a very good chance of going up there," Beauchamp said. "But it will probably wait until Friday. If we get some good numbers, that could be the catalyst to actually push it through. But it can be either way," he added.
Beauchamp pegged initial support at 113-12, and below that at 112-31 which was the top of the previous range that broke on Tuesday.
Other analysts argued that the market was set for consolidation, although the medium term outlook was bullish.

"We fell with prices overextended and back to resistance, some sort of consolidation can be looked for towards the 113-16 area where short term buying opportunities will be offered," said analysts at HSBC Futures in London in a research note.
"We await such moves to go long, or go with breaks of 114-00," they said.
UBS Futures & Options said 114-31 should prove difficult to clear quickly. It cited support at 113-00. By 0800 GMT, September short sterling was two basis points down at 93.18.
